identification: Small Victorian chest of two short over two long drawers, c1860-80, H91 W93 D51 cm (catalogue). Solid top with rounded front edge, plinth base on turned bun feet, turned timber knobs (look original), small brass keyhole escutcheons, a brass lock plate visible on the opened drawer. Top (photo 3 zoomed) is solid plain-sawn timber with cathedral figure, orange-brown colour, consistent with Australian red cedar; drawer fronts have flame/feather figure (cedar flame or mahogany). Drawer linings are pale softwood (pine). Probably Australian colonial cedar as catalogued, possibly Tasmanian; not certain from photos. Finish worn on top and plinth, small marks; no obvious major damage.

viewing_check: Confirm cedar (smell inside drawers, soft reddish grain on drawer sides/back; mahogany is harder and denser), and whether secondaries are pine, cedar or huon pine (huon pine would point to Tasmanian make and add value). Check top for splits or lifting, feet and plinth for replacements, drawer runners and dovetails, and whether knobs are original.
